verified_facts: Composite DTM covers about 99% of England at 1m resolution.
Composite DTM is bare-earth terrain produced by removing surface objects from DSM.
Composite selects newest best-resolution survey where repeats exist.
Composite resampling uses bilinear interpolation before merge where needed.
Composite is supplied in 5km GeoTIFF tiles aligned to OS National Grid.
Elevation is in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and uses OSTN15 transformation.
Individual surveys used in the composite have +/-15cm vertical RMSE.
Time-stamped DTM provides 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m products depending on survey.
Time-stamped metadata identifies survey date, product resolution, transformation and geoidal model.
Transformation is specific to the survey time period.
Point cloud may not exist for every historic DTM/DSM tile due to archiving.
quality_effect: Prevents mixing survey epochs, DSM with DTM, incompatible vertical transformations, or resampled composites without carrying lineage metadata.
